title: Keyboard surface of the settings panel is dead: phase-1 key collection never collects S/arrows/Enter, and S still binds to Set_Lane
evidence:
Collection switch (mouse.odin:80-95) collects only P/Space, D, T, M, Esc: `case .Esc:
				if keys_n < len(keys) { keys[keys_n] = .Esc; keys_n += 1 }
			case: // R/Enter map via the Game_Over early return; phase-2 keys below`. The emit loop's new cases are unreachable: `case .S:
			append(out, Intent(Toggle_Settings{}))` (mouse.odin:152-153), `case .Up:`/`case .Down:` (154-156), and the panel-open `case .S, .Esc:`/`case .Enter:` (127-138). Phase 2 still has `case .S:
			append(out, Intent(Set_Lane{lane = pp.LANE_STANDARD}))` (mouse.odin:388-389). Runtime probe against the copied package: frame1 (S, closed) -> 1 intent `Set_Lane{lane = 1}`, panel_open stays false; frame2 (Down, open) -> 0 intents; frame3 (Enter, open) -> 0 intents; frame4 (Esc, open) -> `Toggle_Settings{}`.
detail: keys[:keys_n] never contains .S/.Up/.Down/.Left/.Right/.Enter, so keyboard users cannot open the panel with S, navigate with arrows, or activate with Enter; S still fires the lane binding. Only Esc works. The panel's own footer says 'S / tap chip to close' — false for keyboard.
recommended_fix: Collect .S/.Up/.Down/.Left/.Right/.Enter in the phase-1 collection switch (enlarge keys[5] to fit) and gate phase-2's `case .S: Set_Lane` so a frame that emitted Toggle_Settings cannot also Set_Lane; re-run input-parity.

title: input_parity_settings_panel passes vacuously on the keyboard leg — its only panel assert is 'ends closed', which a never-opened panel satisfies
detail: The claimed keyboard parity pin cannot fail: S/Down/Enter produce no panel intents (blocker above), the panel never opens on kbd, and 'closed at end' plus an empty command stream both hold. panel_row is never asserted cross-device.
recommended_fix: Assert mid-scenario state, not just end state: e.g. require panel_open==true after the open leg and panel_row==1 after the navigate leg per device (or compare panel_row across devices), so a dead keyboard binding fails the gate.

title: SLA gauge text scales with hud() but sla_row_y pitch and sla_row_rect hit-test do not — overlapping lines and hit/draw divergence at x1.25/x1.50
detail: At x1.25 consecutive gauge lines (20px text on 16px pitch) overlap by ~4px; at x1.50 by ~8px — illegible rows exactly in the mode whose AC is 'chrome stays legible at each step'. The focus-row hit rect also no longer matches the drawn text.
recommended_fix: Route sla_row_y through hud() (e.g. `v.win_h - hud(v, 80) + i32(line) * hud(v, 16)`) and scale sla_row_rect's height/width with hud_f(), keeping draw and hit-test single-sourced like the other panels.

title: crisis.odin re-implements the reduced-motion gate inline instead of routing through pulse_read, the seam the PR calls the single source
detail: The PR body states pulse_read is 'the single seam every animated pulse consumer routes through', but the crisis outline duplicates the PULSE16 read + motion gate. A future change to the gate (e.g. a third state) must be made in two places or the ring and outline diverge.
recommended_fix: Extract a helper that takes the raw phase (e.g. `pulse_at(v, phase)` used by both pulse_read and the crisis outline) or have crisis.odin call a shared gate, so the reduced-motion pin lives in exactly one place.

title: step_of and PALETTE_MODE_COUNT are defined but referenced nowhere
evidence:
`step_of :: proc(scale: f32) -> u8 {` (settings.odin:122) — a repo-wide grep for `step_of` finds only its definition and comment (`// step_of — the nearest step index for a factor (the reverse read for the
// panel display + save).`); the panel display reads snap.ui_scale directly and save uses a11y.scale_step. Likewise `PALETTE_MODE_COUNT :: 4` (app/render/palette.odin:22) has no reference anywhere (grep confirms; the codebase uses `i32(rnd.Palette_Mode.Tritan) + 1` instead, main.odin:758).
detail: Two dead exports introduced by this diff. step_of's comment promises a panel/save use that never landed; PALETTE_MODE_COUNT duplicates the enum-max arithmetic done inline elsewhere. Dead surface invites drift.
recommended_fix: Delete both, or wire them: use PALETTE_MODE_COUNT in the palette-cycle modulo in effect_settings_adjust and step_of where a factor must map back to a step.

title: Settings chip's claimed 'free real estate' (bottom-left) is shared with the SLA gauge block — overlap once 3 gauge rows are visible at x1.25+
detail: Today's 2-class roster keeps the chip exactly adjacent (no overlap at any step), but the third gauge row (9 classes planned) collides at x1.25/x1.50 and the chip silently steals that row's focus clicks. The 'free real estate' claim is stale.
recommended_fix: Either anchor the chip above the SLA block (offset y by the gauge block height) or scale sla_row_y (finding above) and reserve the bottom-left strip for the chip in one shared layout constant.
